security_audit.summary: The static detections are false positives caused by Azure Functions attributes, Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, and advisory text in SKILL.md. remediation.suggestion: Wrap every template in fenced code blocks and label placeholders as non-executable sample values.

remediation.issue: Placeholder URLs appear in several sample snippets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder domains and remind users to replace them with approved internal endpoints.

content.value_statement: Azure Functions projects often fail from timeouts, cold starts, missing bindings, and unsafe runtime choices. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for reliable serverless apps.
actual_capabilities: Explains .NET isolated worker setup with dependency injection and Application Insights.
Shows Node.js v4 and Python v2 trigger patterns.
Describes Durable Functions chaining, fan-out, polling, and queue-based async work.
Highlights production issues such as HTTP timeouts, cold starts, logging gaps, and socket exhaustion.
Provides validation checks for hardcoded secrets, anonymous auth, blocking calls, and missing Function attributes.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not deploy or inspect Azure resources.
Examples use placeholders and require project-specific security review.
Versioned package examples may need updates before production use.
It does not replace Azure documentation or live testing.

use_cases.title: Start a Function App
use_cases.description: Choose the right Azure Functions programming model and set up a production-ready project structure.

use_cases.title: Fix Production Failures
use_cases.description: Diagnose timeout, cold start, logging, binding, and HttpClient lifecycle problems in existing function apps.

use_cases.title: Design Durable Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan orchestration, fan-out, queue, and polling patterns for long-running serverless work.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Runtime
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the best Azure Functions programming model for a new .NET app and explain the required project structure.

prompt_templates.title: Create Async HTTP Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an HTTP trigger pattern that starts long work asynchronously and returns a polling response.

prompt_templates.title: Review Reliability Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Functions design for cold start, timeout, logging, and HttpClient lifecycle risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Durable Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Durable Functions fan-out workflow with retries, poison handling, monitoring, and migration notes for isolated worker.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to start a new .NET function app.
output: Recommends isolated worker for new .NET projects.
Explains dependency injection, HttpClientFactory, and Application Insights setup.
Notes migration risks for in-process apps.

output_examples.input: A team has HTTP functions that time out during long requests.
output: Explains the Azure Load Balancer timeout limit.
Recommends Durable Functions or queue-based async work.
Suggests returning status endpoints for polling.

output_examples.input: An operator sees missing logs and cold start spikes.
output: Checks Application Insights and logging configuration.
Reviews warmup triggers and pre-warmed instance settings.
Identifies blocking calls and heavy startup work.

best_practices: Use isolated worker for new .NET Azure Functions projects.
Use Durable Functions or queues for work that may exceed HTTP limits.
Use managed configuration, Key Vault, and app settings for secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not create a new HttpClient for every invocation.
Do not block async code with Result, Wait, or Thread.Sleep.
Do not use anonymous HTTP authorization in production without another control.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure Functions?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and review prompts for Azure Functions projects.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers .NET isolated worker, Node.js v4, and Python v2 programming models.

faq.question: Does it include Durable Functions patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers chaining, fan-out, polling, queues, and long-running orchestration patterns.

faq.question: Can it find security issues in my repository?
faq.answer: It can guide reviews, but it does not replace static analysis, secret scanning, or manual testing.

faq.question: Are the package versions guaranteed current?
faq.answer: No. Verify package versions against Microsoft documentation before production use.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
